claims.claim_text: Zero DTE options have created a self-reinforcing structural support mechanism for equities that suppresses realized volatility and enables persistent dip-buying, but accumulates hidden tail risk that will eventually discharge catastrophically.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: Zero DTE options allow institutions to cheaply replicate portfolio insurance on a daily basis, removing the incentive to sell equities during drawdowns.
Step 2: Put sellers on the other side collect premium and stay short volatility, reinforcing the market's resistance to sustained selling pressure.
Step 3: Both natural sellers (hedged institutions) and forced sellers (put sellers who haven't been margin called) are neutralized simultaneously, creating structural dip-buying support.
Step 4: The loop's consistent success rewards buy-the-dip behavior, attracting more capital to put-selling strategies and compounding the effect.
Step 5: Apparent volatility compression masks accumulating structural fragility — like a compressed star, the system appears calmer while internal stress builds.
Step 6: When the system eventually breaks, the break will be violent, fast, and V-shaped in recovery — consistent with the pattern of 1987-era portfolio insurance dynamics.
